question.worked_solution:
First, we compute ${B}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${B}^{2}=B,$ so $B$ is an idempotent matrix. 

We can use this fact to compute ${B}^{5}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{5} & ={B}^{2}\cdot {B}^{2}\cdot B \\  & =B\cdot B\cdot B \\  & ={B}^{2}\cdot B \\  & =B\cdot B \\  & ={B}^{2} \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{B}^{5}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$
